correctness.rationale: Normalized spherical moment and exact mixed Wick contractions reduce to a quadratic in first-harmonic energy. Both eigenvalue fourth-power and vector spectral sharp inequalities are simultaneously attained by zonal rank-one data (with dimension-two degeneracy handled). Exact endpoint derivative signs give the two formulas and all extremizers; a monotone positive moment polynomial gives a unique contractivity crossing. Exact coefficient differences prove monotone dimension dependence, and the included direct rational-moment script passes 138 independently expanded finite cases. No finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 1992 unrestricted if-and-only-if radius is not an explicit operator-norm evaluation on a strict mean-zero finite-degree invariant subspace. The 2021 fractional-Laplacian semigroup has multipliers exp(-t sqrt(k(k+d-2))) and is a different operator, so its theorem does not dominate the present claim. At rho above 1/sqrt(3) the global full-space norm exceeds one, while the restricted norm can remain at most one.

originality.rationale: The Beckner 1992 full source concerns a sharp all-functions contraction region but not a norm value for mean-zero degree-one-plus-two inputs beyond that radius; the Montanaro 2012 full Section 2.1 reproduces this general inequality, and a relevant published pure-quadratic result yields only one coefficient of the new optimization. The all-dimensional two-band norm, mixed extremizers, dimension monotonicity and exact restricted threshold are not implied by these statements. The sphere-S² no-damping and Gaussian-limit special cases are recognized as covered. The bibliography remains non-exhaustive.

value.rationale: The restriction to two lowest nonconstant spherical modes is canonical for the Poisson semigroup, and its exact norm controls sharp L2-to-L4 stability rather than only a sufficient full-space bound. The phase change of extremizers, strict dimension dependence, unique best contraction radius and convergence to Gaussian chaos are connected nontrivial structural results, not an unmotivated isolated parameter evaluation.
